data.title: Embracing COP31 as a 'COP of Implementation': Side event explores pathways for global climate diplomacy and cooperation
data.description:
Embracing COP31 as a 'COP of Implementation': Side event explores pathways for global climate diplomacy and cooperation

Embracing COP31 as a 'COP of Implementation': Side event explores pathways for global climate diplomacy and cooperation

PR Newswire

ANKARA, Turkey, Nov. 20, 2026

ANKARA, Turkey, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A thematic side event titled "From Early Warning to Energy Action: Pathways for Global Climate Diplomacy and Cooperation" was held on the afternoon of November 13 local time at the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate during the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

The event was jointly hosted by the United Nations Institute for Training and Research and the Public Meteorological Service Centre of the China Meteorological Administration (National Early Warning Information Release Center), with strategic support from China Energy News, the foreign affairs working committee of the China Energy Research Society (CERS), and the China Institute of Energy Economics Research.

Representatives from Russia, China and various international organizations, including the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), attended the event. Participants held in-depth discussions on climate risk prevention, early warning systems, energy transition and international cooperation, exploring ways to effectively translate climate warnings into concrete energy actions.

At the event, the Climate Leadership Impact (CLI) platform presented its first bilingual report in Chinese and English, titled "From Early Warning to Energy Action: 2026 Innovation Showcase on China's Corporate Actions and Collaborative Practices."

The report highlights how measurable and replicable industrial practices can contribute to COP31's theme of a "COP of Implementation." Focusing on preventing climate disasters and enhancing climate resilience, it explores energy-led approaches to climate action, with the aim of bringing greater certainty and positive momentum to global climate governance.

Joint efforts to translate early warnings into energy action

The World Meteorological Organization's (WMO) State of the Global Climate Update 2026, released during the conference, shows that the global average surface temperature in the first nine months of 2026 was approximately 1.47 degrees above pre-industrial levels. An exceptionally strong El Niño event is expected to further intensify high temperatures and extreme weather, with impacts likely to continue into 2027. The number of countries with multi-hazard early warning systems has increased from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025.

Meanwhile, the UN Environment Programme's Adaptation Gap Report 2026 estimates that developing countries will need approximately $305 billion annually in adaptation financing by 2035. Even if the target of tripling international public adaptation finance is achieved, it would cover only around 20 to 30 percent of the estimated needs. While early warning coverage is expanding, funding, institutional mechanisms and capacity have not kept pace.

Sergey Kononuchenko, special representative of the Russian Foreign Ministry for climate issues and ambassador-at-large, said in his address that climate change is an urgent challenge facing humanity and that the priority now is to translate commitments into concrete action.

He stressed the need to strengthen early warning systems through technological innovation, including artificial intelligence and satellite observation, to protect critical energy infrastructure; uphold multilateralism and ensure developing countries have equitable access to early warning technologies and capacity-building opportunities; and urge all parties, particularly developed countries, to honor their commitments on climate financing and technology transfer. He also recognized China's achievements in building the world's largest renewable energy system and carbon emissions trading market, expressing hope that COP31 would serve as a platform for practical action.

"Early warning is not the end point, but the starting point for action," said Sun Zhengyun, vice chairman and secretary-general of the CERS.

He noted that improvements in forecasting capabilities do not necessarily translate into stronger response capacities. To bridge this gap, Sun said, efforts should first be made to effectively connect climate early warnings with power grid dispatch, renewable energy generation forecasting, energy storage management and emergency response, ensuring that warning information is genuinely incorporated into energy system operations.

Climate risk management should also be strengthened in energy planning and investment decisions to improve the resilience of projects from the outset. In addition, international cooperation should be deepened, with greater emphasis on capacity building in developing countries, enabling more regions to develop comprehensive capabilities to translate early warnings into action.

Xie Rongbin, Party secretary, chairman and editor-in-chief of China Energy and Automobile Media Group Co Ltd, president of China Automotive News, and editor-in-chief of China Energy News, said the global energy transition is a systemic transformation requiring the coordinated management of climate risk early warnings, technological innovation, industrial collaboration, market mechanisms, security safeguards and equitable development.

The key, Xie said, is to turn early warning capabilities into effective emergency responses. China is actively exploring ways to integrate meteorological warnings with energy dispatch, while using technology to strengthen the resilience of energy systems against extreme weather shocks. In July this year, China's installed solar power capacity surpassed that of coal-fired power, making solar the country's largest source of installed power capacity.

Andrew Tupper, head of the Early Warning Services at the WMO, expressed agreement with this approach. He noted that conventional, general-purpose weather warnings are no longer sufficient to meet current needs. There is an urgent need to establish "impact-based early warning systems" that connect meteorological information with energy operations, enabling warnings to trigger timely and targeted protective measures for energy assets.

Bridging meteorology and energy through cross-sector collaboration

As a core member of the research team behind the report From Climate Early Warnings to Energy Action: 2026 Progress Report on Chinese Enterprises' Actions and Collaborative Practices, Dr. Wang Jingyu, assistant director of the national key laboratory of advanced electromagnetic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and an associate research fellow, presented the CLI platform's first bilingual report in Chinese and English.

Wang said the report features 16 practical case studies across six categories, covering renewable energy output forecasting, infrastructure protection, power grid dispatch and maintenance, energy security for key users, supply-demand adjustment, and emissions reduction and carbon sequestration.

Ye Dong, a senior researcher at the Public Meteorological Service Centre of the China Meteorological Administration, introduced initiatives to harness AI for energy-related meteorological and climate services under the theme "From Accurate Forecasting to Enhanced Climate Resilience."

Ye noted that meteorological conditions have a profound impact on the entire energy chain, from production and transmission to consumption. As global climate change intensifies, extreme weather poses increasingly prominent threats to energy systems. Meanwhile, non-disaster weather conditions with significant impacts, such as prolonged periods of weak winds and reduced sunshine, can also cause fluctuations in renewable energy output and disrupt the balance between electricity supply and demand.

Specialized meteorological early warning services for the energy sector are therefore essential to ensuring energy security and strengthening the climate resilience of energy systems, Ye said.

China is actively developing AI-based meteorological forecasting models tailored to energy-sector applications, drawing on domestically developed satellites and multi-source observation data. Ye stressed that AI is merely a technological tool, and that the key is to address real-world operational needs and translate accurate weather forecasts and warnings into concrete measures for protecting energy facilities, power dispatch and risk response.

Practical applications on the power grid side have already established a complete chain from forecasting to response. State Grid Shaanxi Electric Power, drawing on standardized observation systems at power stations and the "Fuxi" meteorological foundation model, has achieved an accuracy rate of 95.2 percent in short-term power output forecasting. Its icing warnings now provide an additional 18 hours of lead time, while the initiative has cumulatively enabled an additional 65.05 million kilowatt-hours of renewable electricity generation.

State Grid Zhoushan Power Supply Company in East China's Zhejiang Province has used a large AI model to coordinate preparations before disasters, emergency response during disasters and post-disaster repairs, reducing the average time needed to complete the fault-resolution process from eight hours to 4.7 hours.

On the enterprise side, early warnings are being translated into economic returns and asset protection. China Resources Power Technology Institute has developed an integrated climate and energy storage management platform. Based on operational data from a wind power project equipped with energy storage in Central China's Hubei Province during the first half of this year, the platform is estimated to reduce renewable energy curtailment by 92.6 percent and increase overall economic benefits by more than 10 million yuan.

Trina Solar has integrated module protection, grid-forming energy storage, and intelligent operation and maintenance. Estimates based on a 100-megawatt solar project in Texas, the US, indicate that the approach could reduce average annual asset losses by 94 percent, demonstrating the potential for similar solutions to be replicated in overseas regions facing high climate risks.

Policy support is also creating an institutional framework for closer coordination between meteorology and the energy sector. In January this year, the China Meteorological Administration and the National Energy Administration jointly issued guidelines on developing an energy meteorological service system, setting out 20 tasks and aiming to establish an integrated energy meteorological service system covering all energy-sector scenarios by 2027.

Tian Yuyang, assistant director of the foreign affairs working committee of the CERS, said the CLI platform would continue to advance its work across four areas: risk governance and financial support, AI-enabled forecasting and decision-making, coordinated clean energy dispatch, and interdisciplinary talent development. The goal is to translate research findings into operational applications and turn pilot experience into industry standards.

Under the theme "How can meteorological warnings be effectively translated into action within energy systems?" three representatives of international organizations – Tupper, Avishek Malla, head of renewable energy at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), and Binu Parthan, deputy director of country engagement and partnerships at IRENA – joined enterprise representatives, including Wu Xiao, vice president of Trina Solar and head of the group's ESG management and risk control, and Han Shutong, general manager of LONGi Green Energy Technology's UK representative office, for an in-depth discussion. The session was moderated by He Chaoxin, chief youth officer of the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate.

Tupper pointed out that the bottleneck in cross-sector collaboration lies not in information sharing itself, but in whether energy departments genuinely rely on meteorological warnings when making dispatch decisions. Without trust built through long-term cooperation, warnings may remain merely reference information rather than becoming a basis for decision-making.

The WMO is now incorporating this model of trust-based collaboration into its global early warning framework, promoting a shift from basic cooperation between meteorological and energy departments toward substantive operational coordination, Tupper said.

Malla presented practical achievements in mountainous areas of South Asia. ICIMOD has established a multi-tiered early warning system that includes high-resolution forecasts up to 54 hours ahead, flood forecasts 10 to 15 days in advance and glacial lake outburst monitoring. Information is shared with government departments and local communities, while text messages and alerts are used to deliver warnings directly to the public.

The center is also incorporating climate data into sensitivity analysis models used by hydropower investors and commercial banks, opening up new channels for integrating climate information into risk assessments of energy infrastructure.

Parthan focused on the implementation stage after warnings are issued. Taking heatwaves as an example, he noted that high temperatures both reduce the transmission capacity of power lines and drive up electricity demand for cooling. However, such warning information has not yet been effectively incorporated into the operational planning of utility companies.

He proposed bringing together multiple stakeholders, including power grid planners, government departments, system operators and financial institutions, to establish cross-sector mechanisms for short-term decision-making. This would enable early warning information to directly inform real-time energy system dispatch and investment decisions.

Participants agreed that the main bottleneck in translating early warnings into action is shifting from meteorological technology to the operational rules of energy systems. The CLI platform's first progress report is a response to this challenge. By turning the practical experience of Chinese enterprises in dispatch response, resilience upgrades and cross-border cooperation into measurable and replicable industry references, the report aims to help transform COP31's theme of a "COP of Implementation" from a conference slogan into concrete action within energy systems.

During the conference, China's approaches also offered developing countries new options for addressing gaps in their climate response capabilities.

On November 11, China's AI-powered meteorological early warning solution, the "Mazu" all-in-one system, was unveiled to a global audience at a high-level forum on South-South cooperation on climate change. As of October 2026, the system had been deployed in eight countries, including Pakistan, Ethiopia and Sri Lanka, and was undergoing cloud-based trials in more than 50 countries.

On November 12, He Yang, deputy head of the National Energy Administration, said at a high-level event on the Global Grid Accelerator initiative that China was willing to support countries in building power grids that ensure energy security and prosperity through a model of "shared provision."

data.title: Vinci Gets $439 Million Contract to Build LNG Tank in Canada
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Vinci said it has been awarded a contract valued at around 400 million euros ($438.7 million) to build a new liquefied natural gas tank in Canada.

The French construction and infrastructure group said Friday that the contract, from JGC Fluor BC LNG II Joint Venture, will see it build a 225,000 cubic meter tank for the LNG Canada liquefied natural gas export terminal in Kitimat, British Columbia.

The contract is part of LNG Canada's Phase 2 expansion and comes after Vinci completed the site's first 225,000 cubic meter tank in 2025.

Write to Dominic Chopping at dominic.chopping@wsj.com

data.title: Leads Biolabs Presents Opamtistomig (PD-L1/4-1BB Bispecific Antibody) to Global Investors at the 2026 Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference
data.description:
NANJING, China, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Nanjing Leads Biolabs Co., Ltd. ("Leads Biolabs" or the "Company," Stock Code: 9887.HK) presented the differentiated profile of opamtistomig (LBL-024) to global pharmaceutical companies and investors at the 2026 Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference in London, underscoring the therapy's global competitiveness in next-generation immuno-oncology (IO 2.0).

Dr. Kang Xiaoqiang, the Company's founder, Chairman and CEO, delivered the invited presentation. He built it around three lines of evidence: the mechanism and clinical evidence behind long-tail survival, activity across tumor types, and safety.

The clinical data support opamtistomig's potential as a pan-tumor IO 2.0 backbone therapy with durable survival benefit. Results from multiple trials point to activity in settings where conventional immunotherapy has limited reach. Those include low response rates, immunologically "cold" tumors, and tumors with negative or low PD-L1 expression. Deep responses in major indications and a doubling of median overall survival (OS) versus historical data in refractory cold tumors reinforce that positioning. Together, the findings outline five dimensions of value for a next-generation immunotherapy backbone.
(1) Long-term survival potential and managing cancer as a chronic disease: every indication with sufficiently long follow-up — including first-line combination chemotherapy and last-line monotherapy — has shown long-tail survival benefit. Median OS in extrapulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma (EP-NEC) doubled compared with historical data. In small cell lung cancer (SCLC), median OS remains immature at 18 months of follow-up. Among the first 18 patients with NSCLC, follow-up has passed 12 months and the survival trend is encouraging. With mature follow-up, monotherapy also produced markedly longer OS in later-line biliary tract cancer (BTC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), ovarian cancer (OC) and other cold tumors. The findings suggest advanced cancer may become a chronic disease managed over the long term.
(2) Broad-spectrum efficacy: to date, breakthrough efficacy has been demonstrated in seven tumor types, supporting the potential to become a next-generation broad-spectrum immunotherapy backbone.
(3) Breakthroughs in cold tumors: to date, breakthrough efficacy has been demonstrated in five immunologically cold tumor types, offering the potential to overcome the efficacy limitations of first-generation immunotherapy.
(4) Coverage across patient populations: consistent trends of benefit have been observed in patients with positive, negative and low PD-L1 expression, offering the potential to cover a broader patient population.
(5) Excellent safety: more than 800 patients have received treatment, with no dose-limiting toxicities observed. The overall safety profile is similar to that of PD-(L)1 monoclonal antibodies, supporting long-term administration in broader patient populations.

At the conference, Leads Biolabs disclosed for the first time plans to launch several ADC combination programs in 2027. The programs include combinations with its in-house next-generation bispecific ADCs and T-cell engager ADCs (TCE-ADCs), as well as with ADCs from leading industry players.

Long-Tail Survival: A Mechanism Built on Long-Lived Memory T Cells

Opamtistomig is built with high affinity for PD-L1 and very low affinity for 4-1BB. The design enables conditional 4-1BB activation in the tumor microenvironment. Checkpoint blockade and co-stimulation therefore occur only within the tumor microenvironment. While avoiding hepatotoxicity caused by 4-1BB activation in normal tissues, this design reshapes the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. It significantly promotes T-cell activation and proliferation, stimulates abundant cytokine secretion and substantially reduces the number of regulatory T cells. Most importantly, it generates long-lived memory T cells. Those cells continue immune surveillance after treatment stops, which is the fundamental basis for opamtistomig’s ability to overcome the limitations of conventional immunotherapy and deliver durable survival benefits to patients.


Figure 1. Opamtistomig drives accumulation of 4-1BB-positive cells in tumors and markedly expands CD8+ T cells.

Clinical Data: Median OS Doubled in EP-NEC, with Long-Tail Trends in SCLC and Three Other Tumor Types

EP-NEC is the indication with the most mature survival data for opamtistomig. Long-term survival data have been reported from both first-line and heavily pretreated studies (2026 ESMO late-breaking abstract and selected oral presentation data).

In the pivotal registrational study of opamtistomig monotherapy in third-line or later EP-NEC (n=96), median follow-up was 16.3 months. Median OS was 8.7 months, versus approximately 3-4 months in historical data.

In first-line EP-NEC with combination chemotherapy (n=69), median follow-up was 21.2 months. Median OS was immature, and the 18-month OS rate was 55.7%. Historical median OS with first-line chemotherapy was 11.5-12.5 months.

In small cell lung cancer (SCLC), median follow-up has reached 18 months. OS data remain immature, and the long-term survival trend is encouraging. In monotherapy cohorts of heavily pretreated patients from an early basket trial, follow-up has passed two years and OS data are mature. All three tumor types showed encouraging long-tail benefit trends.

In third-line or later biliary tract cancer (BTC) (n=31), median OS was 7.5 months as a third-line or later treatment, numerically exceeding historical second-line data of 6.2 months with mFOLFOX and 5.3 months with regorafenib. In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) previously treated with immunotherapy (n=14), median OS was 13.3 months. Historical second-line data were 10.6 months with regorafenib and 10.2 months with cabozantinib. In second-line or later ovarian cancer (OC) (n=11), median OS was 26.5 months. Historical second-line data with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy were 13.3 months.

The conference also included updated follow-up for the first 18 patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Follow-up reached 12.3 months, and responses continued to deepen. The data also point to long-tail potential.

All subtypes showed responses lasting longer than historical median progression-free survival (PFS) for standard treatment in the same indication. Every patient still on treatment had maintained a response for about 12 months. Historical median PFS was approximately 3-4 months in immunotherapy-pretreated non-squamous NSCLC, 8-9 months in first-line non-squamous NSCLC and about 7 months in first-line squamous NSCLC.

Prolonged responses were seen in PD-L1-positive and squamous populations. Two PD-L1-positive patients with first-line non-squamous disease and five patients with first-line squamous disease had each remained on treatment for more than 357 days. All were still on treatment. The Company views these durations as a meaningful survival signal and sees competitive potential against other bispecific antibodies.

Many patients remained in response at longer follow-up. The Company had presented these 18 patients at the 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC), when median follow-up was about 10 months. Compared with that update, nine patients remained on treatment at the longer follow-up and only two additional progressions were recorded. That pattern is consistent with the course of cancer treatment.


Figure 2. Updated follow-up data for 18 patients with NSCLC presented at the Company's first R&D Day on Oct. 31, 2025 (Cohort 1A: immunotherapy-pretreated non-squamous NSCLC; Cohort 2A: first-line non-squamous NSCLC; Cohort 2B: first-line squamous NSCLC).

Broad Activity: Responses in Seven Tumor Types and Six Oral Presentations at Major Congresses

Responses have been observed repeatedly in seven indications, including the major indication of NSCLC and five immunologically "cold" tumor types. Studies have been selected six times for oral presentations at leading international oncology congresses, including the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO), the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and the World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC).


Figure 3. Opamtistomig has received seven global regulatory designations and marketing application acceptances, and has been selected for six oral presentations at leading international oncology congresses.

First-Line NSCLC (2026 WCLC Oral Presentation Data)
In the squamous cohort (n=31), median follow-up was 7.4 months. The objective response rate (ORR) was 87.1% and the disease control rate (DCR) was 96.8%. The six-month PFS rate reached 86.7%. Patients with positive and negative PD-L1 expression showed consistent benefit trends. ORRs were 84.6% and 88.2%, respectively. Six-month PFS rates were 84.6% and 87.4%, respectively.

In the non-squamous cohort (n=31), median follow-up was 6.9 months. ORR was 54.8% and DCR was 93.5%. In the PD-L1-positive subgroup, ORR reached 81.8% and DCR reached 100.0%. The six-month PFS rate reached 90.0%. Responses were also seen in patients with low PD-L1 expression, with a tumor proportion score of 1%-49%.

First-Line BTC (2026 ESMO Poster Data)
In the overall population (n=20), median follow-up was 8.6 months. ORR was 70.0% and DCR was 95%. Median PFS was 8.0 months, and the six-month OS rate was 90.0%. In the PD-L1-positive subgroup, ORR was 100.0% and the six-month OS rate was 100.0%. In the PD-L1-negative subgroup, ORR was 50.0% and DCR was 91.7%. Median PFS was 7.2 months, and the six-month OS rate was 83.3%.

First-Line HCC
Data were updated with a larger sample and longer follow-up than the 2026 interim results disclosure. In the overall population (n=23), median follow-up was approximately seven months. ORR was 43.5% and DCR was 82.6%. In the PD-L1-positive subgroup, ORR was 50% and DCR was 75%. The subgroup grew from five to 12 patients since the 2026 interim results, with the response level holding steady.

First-Line Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC)
Data were updated with longer follow-up than the 2026 interim results disclosure. In the overall population (n=20), median follow-up was approximately 5.5 months. ORR was 70% and DCR was 90%. In the PD-L1-positive subgroup, ORR was 77.8% and DCR was 100%.

Platinum-Resistant OC
In the overall population (n=12), median follow-up was approximately 2.5 months. ORR was 16.7% and DCR was 66.7%. Neither median PFS nor median OS had been reached. In the PD-L1-positive subgroup, ORR was 40% and DCR was 80%. Neither median PFS nor median OS had been reached.

First-Line SCLC
ORR was 88.1% and DCR was 96.6%. As of October 2026, median follow-up was 18 months and OS data remained immature.

EP-NEC
Data from multiple clinical studies of monotherapy in previously treated EP-NEC demonstrated consistent benefits across lines of therapy. In second-line, second-line or later, and third-line or later settings, ORRs were 38.1%, 33.3% and 26.0%, respectively. Median PFS was 4.1, 2.8 and 1.4 months, respectively. Median OS was 11.8, 11.9 and 8.7 months, respectively.

In first-line EP-NEC with combination chemotherapy, ORR was 69.2% and DCR was 90.8%. Median PFS was 5.7 months. Median OS was immature, and the 18-month OS rate was 55.7%.

Safety: More Than 800 Patients Treated With No Dose-Limiting Toxicities

Hepatotoxicity has long limited the clinical use of 4-1BB agonists. Opamtistomig's conditional 4-1BB activation is designed to address that challenge at the mechanistic level. To date, more than 800 patients have received opamtistomig across 14 indications. No dose-limiting toxicities have been observed. The maximum tolerated dose was not reached even with dose escalation to 25 mg/kg. Safety and tolerability were similar across monotherapy and combination trials. The overall safety profile was similar to that of PD-(L)1 monoclonal antibodies. Those findings support longer-term dosing in broader populations and further study of combination regimens.

Building on the responses seen with opamtistomig plus chemotherapy in cold tumors, the Company plans to test combinations with antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). The approach retains the targeted cytotoxic effect of ADCs while using the immune system to clear tumor cells. The goal is a next-generation standard of care. Combinations under consideration include opamtistomig with an EGFR/PD-L1 ADC, a CDH17/CD3/ADC and a DLL3/CD3/ADC, as well as several ADCs from leading industry players. Beyond ADC combinations, the Company also plans to explore regimens with other molecules, including anti-VEGF agents and T-cell engagers (TCEs), to establish new standards of care in specific tumor types.


Figure 4. Planned combination studies for opamtistomig.

During the conference, the Company's senior management held a series of closed-door, one-on-one business development and investor meetings. Discussions with overseas institutions covered registration timelines by indication, global clinical development plans, commercialization strategy and pipeline synergies.

Executive Commentary

"Taking part in Jefferies was about more than sharing clinical data," said Dr. Kang Xiaoqiang, founder, Chairman and CEO of Leads Biolabs. "It let us present the full logic behind our differentiated innovation to global investors and industry partners. It also helped advance our global registration plans and international partnerships.

"Cancer immunotherapy has entered the IO 2.0 era. Opamtistomig's value lies in a manageable safety profile and the potential for long overall survival benefit across tumor types. Together, those features offer a new treatment framework in areas that conventional immunotherapy has struggled to reach."

About the Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference
Hosted by U.S. investment bank Jefferies, the Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference is one of the world's largest healthcare investment summits. The 2026 invitation-only meeting took place Nov. 16-19 at The Waldorf Hilton, London and ME London, alongside London Life Sciences Week. The conference covers biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, medical devices and healthcare services. Company presentations, one-to-one and small-group investor meetings, and panel discussions focus on near- and longer-term investment opportunities and industry trends in global healthcare.

About Opamtistomig
Opamtistomig (LBL-024) is emerging as a next-generation pan-cancer backbone therapy with potential overall survival (OS) benefit that simultaneously targets PD-L1 and the co-stimulatory receptor 4-1BB. Currently, opamtistomig is being evaluated in 14 indications, including one pivotal single-arm registrational study, one confirmatory Phase III study, and nine proof-of-concept studies, covering major indications such as NSCLC and multiple cold tumors. To date, opamtistomig has demonstrated robust antitumor activity across seven tumor types—extrapulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma (EP-NEC), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), small cell lung cancer (SCLC), biliary tract cancer (BTC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), and ovarian cancer (OC)—highlighting its clinical value and broad therapeutic promise.

Developed using Leads Biolabs’ proprietary X-body bispecific platform, opamtistomig is designed to simultaneously block PD-1/PD-L1 immune suppression and conditionally activate 4-1BB, an agonist pathway, resulting in a potent and synergistic anti-tumor immune response. It has a safety profile comparable to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors and demonstrates broader-spectrum anti-cancer potential. Mechanistically, 4-1BB agonism can reactivate exhausted T cells and promote robust T-cell proliferation, offering significant promise for PD-1/PD-L1–resistant or immunologically “cold” tumors and potentially offering durable survival benefits.

Recognizing its clinical potential in EP-NEC, opamtistomig received Breakthrough Therapy Designation from China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) in October 2024, Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in November 2024, Fast Track Designation from the FDA and ODD from the European Commission in January 2026, and ODD from Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) in September 2026. In October 2026, the FDA granted a second Fast Track Designation, this one for first-line advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer.

In July 2026, its New Drug Application (NDA) was granted priority review designation by the NMPA, followed by NDA acceptance in August 2026, positioning opamtistomig as a potential world's first approved 4-1BB-targeting antibody, the first approved agonist antibody, and the first approved treatment for EP-NEC.

About Leads Biolabs
Founded in 2012, Leads Biolabs is a clinical-stage biotechnology company dedicated to the discovery, development, and commercialization of innovative therapies to address underserved medical needs in oncology, autoimmune, and other severe diseases both in China and globally.

data.title: U.K. Government Borrowed More in October, But Stays on Track for Smaller Deficit — Update
data.description:
By Paul Hannon

The U.K. government borrowed more in October than a year earlier, but it remained on course to reduce its budget deficit in the current fiscal year.

The Office for National Statistics on Friday said government spending exceeded revenues by 17 billion pounds ($22.25 billion) in October, an increase of 800 million pounds from the same month of 2025.

The increase in borrowing partly reflected a rise in interest costs as inflation and bond yields picked up since the start of the war between the U.S. and Iran.

In October, interest payments totaled 11.2 billion pounds, an increase of 2.8 billion pounds from the same month last year.

"Much of the deficit is out of the government's control, with the war in the Middle East continuing to put pressure on inflation and the economy," said Kit Rees, an investment strategist at Quilter.

Over the first seven months of the fiscal year that will end in early April, borrowing was 111.3 billion pounds, down 7.3 billion pounds from the same period a year earlier.

At 3.5% of gross domestic product, the budget deficit for the fiscal year to October was lower than the 3.8% recorded a year earlier.

The government's total debt stood at 3.1 trillion pounds, or 95.8% of GDP, up from 93.9% in October 2025.

In its October budget, the government set out plans for spending and taxation that aim to reduce the budget deficit further in the current and subsequent fiscal years. However, borrowing is set to be higher than previously targeted.

For this year, the Office for Budget Responsibility estimates the budget deficit will be 4.2% of gross domestic product, a large increase from the 3.6% planned in March.

The overshoot partly reflects the increased costs of providing government services as energy prices have risen since the start of the war. Higher prices are also raising the cost of paying interest, since the U.K. has a higher share of bonds with payouts linked to inflation than its peers.

data.title: Sailun Group Attends COP31, Showcasing Green Practices Driven by Technological Innovation
data.description:
Sailun Group Attends COP31, Showcasing Green Practices Driven by Technological Innovation

Sailun Group Attends COP31, Showcasing Green Practices Driven by Technological Innovation

PR Newswire

ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 20, 2026

ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) was held in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20. As a representative of the green transformation of the rubber and tire industry, Sailun Group was invited to attend the conference, where Chairwoman Yanhua Liu shared the company's innovative practices and achievements in climate action and sustainable development.

Guided by its ESG principles, Sailun Group continues to leverage technological innovation to explore low-carbon development pathways across the entire life cycle of rubber tires, delivering practical and scalable solutions. Liu noted that Sailun originated from Qingdao University of Science and Technology, and that technological innovation and sustainability have been embedded in its corporate DNA since its founding.

After more than a decade of R&D, Sailun pioneered Eco Point3 Tires, achieving green, low-carbon, and sustainable development throughout the product life cycle, from raw material selection and manufacturing to product use. The technology also enhances three key performance attributes—wet handling, low rolling resistance, and wear resistance—overcoming the century-old "Magic Triangle" challenge in the tire industry while significantly reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions.

Liu emphasized that sustainability gives a new meaning to a "good tire": safer for drivers, more resource-efficient, and more environmentally friendly. Through technological innovation, Sailun is contributing practical solutions from the rubber industry to global climate action.

As a member of the United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD), Sailun actively participates in global climate initiatives. Sailun currently holds an AA rating in the MSCI ESG Ratings, placing it among the leading companies in the global tire industry. It is also the first tire company in China to have its science-based emissions reduction targets validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), leveraging technological innovation to accelerate the green and low-carbon transformation of the global tire industry.

With its global footprint, Sailun is evolving from a participant to an explorer and driver of global climate action. Liu stated that Sailun will continue to focus on customer needs and leverage advanced technologies and quality services to provide safe, comfortable, and energy-efficient products and services to customers worldwide.

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026

New Las Vegas Book Reveals the Extraordinary Story of a Magician, a Million-Dollar Gambler, and the Casinos That Never Saw Him Coming

Advance Orders Now Open for ROSENBLATT — Coming January 15, 2027

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Las Vegas has produced its share of legendary gamblers, con men, hustlers, and thieves. But few stories are quite like ROSENBLATT, a provocative new book about a man who went from having almost nothing to becoming one of the highest-stakes gamblers in Las Vegas history — without ever risking a dollar of his own money.

He robbed casinos without a gun. He became a million-dollar player. He was eventually barred from virtually every casino in town.

And for years, nobody knew exactly what he had done.

The casinos knew they'd been hit. They never learned how much. They never learned when, and they never learned how.

At the center of the story is Darryl Rosenblatt, a magician whose greatest illusion wasn't performed on a stage. It was performed in plain sight, under the watchful eyes of casino executives, surveillance operators, and some of the most sophisticated security systems in the world.

What began as a remarkable talent for deception became a life of enormous wagers, extraordinary characters, spectacular excess, and ultimately, prison.

But ROSENBLATT is far more than a story about stealing from casinos.

It is the story of an unlikely rise through the underbelly of American life, where survival demanded ingenuity, rules were negotiable, and the difference between a magician and a criminal sometimes depended on who was watching.

Written with biting humor, unapologetic candor, and an insider's knowledge of a Las Vegas most visitors will never see, ROSENBLATT takes readers on a roller coaster ride through three decades of Vegas depravity through the rapier lens of a damaged man.

There are no fictional masterminds here. No Hollywood heists. No masked men running through casino floors with bags of cash.

The theft was the illusion.

And the casinos were the audience.

"Everything in his life had been preparing him for Las Vegas. Las Vegas was not prepared for him."

Scheduled for release January 15, 2027, ROSENBLATT is now available for advance purchase ahead of its official publication.

For readers fascinated by the hidden history of Las Vegas, high-stakes gambling, organized deception, and extraordinary true-life characters, this is a story that challenges everything they think they know about the casino business.

He didn't hide the money. He hid the Crime.

And now, for the first time, he's telling the story.

data.title: GenSight Biologics Announces Successful EUR 1.1 Million Fundraising Supported by Existing Shareholders
data.description:
GenSight Biologics Announces Successful EUR 1.1 Million Fundraising Supported by Existing Shareholders

Regulatory News:

NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY, IN THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, CANADA, AUSTRALIA, JAPAN AND SOUTH AFRICA

GenSight Biologics ("GenSight" or the "Company") (Euronext: SIGHT, ISIN: FR0013183985, PEA-PME eligible), a biopharma company focused on developing and commercializing innovative gene therapies for retinal neurodegenerative diseases and central nervous system disorders, today announced the successful completion of a EUR 1,100,000.19 fundraising subscribed by two of its existing shareholders, Heights Capital and Invus (the "Fundraising"), to be paid in full in cash. The Fundraising follows a similar structure of shares and warrants, including pre-funded warrants, to the financings conducted in March and October 2026, as further detailed below.

The Fundraising is subject neither to the obligation to publish a prospectus pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 June 2017, as amended (the "Prospectus Regulation"), requiring an approval from the French Financial Markets Authority (Autorité des marchés financiers – the "AMF"), nor to the obligation to publish and file with the AMF a document containing the information set out in Appendix IX of the Prospectus Regulation, in each case for the purpose of the listing on the regulated market of Euronext in Paris ("Euronext Paris") of the Offered Shares, the Pre-Funded Warrant Shares and the Investor Warrant Shares (as defined below) to be issued in the context of the Fundraising.

Use of proceeds

The gross proceeds of the Fundraising amount to EUR 1.1 million, with net proceeds of approximately EUR 1.05 million.

The cash proceeds will be used to finance the Company's operating activities and working capital requirements, in addition to revenues from the early access programs, pending the structural financing of the RECOVER Phase 3 trial.

This financing, supplementing the October 2026 fundraising, covers the near-term funding requirement of up to EUR 2 million disclosed on September 29 and October 7, 2026. This will enable the Company to fund its operations until late March 2027, when the first significant payments related to the preparation of the RECOVER trial fall due. This also remains subject to the number of patients treated under the French named patient early access program (AAC) being in line with the Company's estimates.

The Company's cash flow projections do not assume any exercise of the warrants issued in this Fundraising. If all such warrants were exercised, the Company would receive additional gross proceeds of approximately EUR 0.93 million.

"With this financing, we have completed, on schedule, the approximately €2 million raise we announced with our half-year results," said Jan Eryk Umiastowski, Chief Financial Officer of GenSight Biologics. "We are grateful to Invus and Heights, who have been among our most consistent supporters since November 2024, for standing alongside GenSight once again. Their renewed commitment allows us to approach our upcoming interactions with regulatory agencies with confidence, while we continue to make GS010/LUMEVOQ available to patients through early access and prepare a structural financing for the next phase of its development."

Terms and conditions of the Fundraising

The Fundraising was carried out through the issuance, without preferential subscription rights and without a priority subscription period, of:

  1. 4,237,288 ordinary shares (actions ordinaires), with a par value of EUR 0.025 per share of the Company (the "Offered Shares");
  2. 13,157,898 pre-funded warrants (the "Offered Pre-Funded Warrants") giving the right to subscribe for 13,157,898 additional ordinary shares (the "Pre-Funded Warrant Shares"); and
  3. 17,395,186 warrants (the "Offered Investor Warrants") giving the right to subscribe for 8,697,593 additional ordinary shares (the "Investor Warrant Shares").

Investors had the choice to subscribe for two "units" composed of:

  • Offered Shares to which Offered Investor Warrants were attached (the "ABSA"), with one Offered Investor Warrant attached to each Offered Share, or
  • Offered Pre-Funded Warrants to which Offered Investor Warrants were attached (the "Pre-Paid Units"), with one Offered Investor Warrant attached to each Offered Pre-Funded Warrant.

One Offered Pre-Funded Warrant gives the investor the right to subscribe for one Pre-Funded Warrant Share, and two Offered Investor Warrants give the investor the right to subscribe for one Investor Warrant Share.

The Offered Investor Warrants attached to the Offered Shares and to the Offered Pre-Funded Warrants are identical and thus fungible when they are detached from the Offered Shares and the Offered Pre-Funded Warrants, upon issuance. They will not be fungible with the warrants issued in the Company's previous financings.

The Pre-Funded Warrant Shares and the Investor Warrant Shares (together, the "New Shares") are fungible with the Company's existing ordinary shares of EUR 0.025 par value.

The Fundraising was decided on November 19, 2026 by the Chief Executive Officer, pursuant to the delegation of competence granted to her by the Company's board of directors (the "Board of Directors") on November 13, 2026. The Board of Directors acted pursuant to the delegation of competence granted to it under the 19th resolution of the Company's shareholders' meeting held on May 19, 2026 (the "General Meeting"). The ABSA and the Pre-Paid Units were issued in a capital increase with cancellation of shareholders' preferential subscription rights for the benefit of investors within the category of persons defined by the 19th resolution of the General Meeting, in accordance with Article L. 225-138 of the French Commercial Code, to be paid up in cash.

The issue price of one ABSA is EUR 0.0708.

The issue price of one Pre-Paid Unit is EUR 0.0608.

The exercise price of one Offered Investor Warrant is EUR 0.04565, i.e. EUR 0.0913 per Investor Warrant Share.

The exercise price of one Offered Pre-Funded Warrant is EUR 0.01 per Pre-Funded Warrant Share.

The EUR 0.0708 issue price of one ABSA represents a facial discount of 7% (i.e. EUR 0.0053) to the last closing price of the Company's shares on Euronext Paris on November 19, 2026, i.e. EUR 0.0761 (the "Closing Price").

The exercise price of two Offered Investor Warrants represents a 20% premium to the Closing Price.

The issue price of two ABSA, less twice the EUR 0.0109 theoretical value of one Offered Investor Warrant1, plus the exercise price per share of such Offered Investor Warrants, represents an average subscription price of EUR 0.0704 for each of the three New Shares issued (the two Offered Shares and the Investor Warrant Share), above the Closing Price less the maximum facial discount of 20% provided for in the 19th resolution of the General Meeting.

The same applies to the Pre-Paid Units.

The Offered Pre-Funded Warrants may be exercised at any time within 60 months of their issuance. The Offered Investor Warrants may be exercised at any time within 60 months of their issuance.

In the event all Offered Investor Warrants and all Offered Pre-Funded Warrants are exercised, their exercise would generate additional gross proceeds of EUR 925,669.22 (i.e. EUR 131,578.98 for the Pre-Funded Warrant Shares and EUR 794,090.24 for the Investor Warrant Shares).

Impact of the Fundraising on the Company's shareholding

Following the issuance of the Offered Shares, the Company's total share capital will be EUR 6,261,365.45 (composed of 250,454,618 ordinary shares). If all the Offered Pre-Funded Warrants are exercised, and thus all the Pre-Funded Warrant Shares issued, the Company's total share capital will be EUR 6,590,312.90 (composed of 263,612,516 ordinary shares). If all the Offered Investor Warrants are exercised, and thus all the Investor Warrant Shares issued, the Company's total share capital will be EUR 6,807,752.73 (composed of 272,310,109 ordinary shares).

Please see:

  • sections 19.1.3, 19.1.4 and 19.1.5 of GenSight's 2025 Universal Registration Document and Notes 10 and 17 to the half-year financial statements for the six-month period ended June 30, 2026 and paragraph 2.G of the Half Year Financial Report for that period; and
  • the press releases issued on October 8, 2026 and October 16, 2026 relating to the EUR 1.0 million fundraising,

About GenSight Biologics S.A.

GenSight Biologics S.A. is a clinical-stage biopharma company focused on developing and commercializing innovative gene therapies for retinal neurodegenerative diseases and central nervous system disorders. GenSight Biologics' pipeline leverages two core technology platforms, the Mitochondrial Targeting Sequence (MTS) and optogenetics, to help preserve or restore vision in patients suffering from blinding retinal diseases. GenSight Biologics' lead product candidate, GS010 (lenadogene nolparvovec), is in Phase 3 in Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy (LHON), a rare mitochondrial disease that leads to irreversible blindness in teens and young adults. GS010 is currently in clinical development, has not to date been granted marketing authorization in France or any other jurisdiction, and is therefore not available commercially. Using its gene therapy-based approach, GenSight Biologics' product candidates are designed to be administered in a single treatment to each eye by intravitreal injection to offer patients a sustainable functional visual recovery.
